issues.title: Ready quotation waits for an already-speaking acknowledgment
issues.found_on: Original GoLive through native SIP adapter
issues.symptom: One readout takes 7530 ms: tool execution 4162 ms, then ready-result gap wait 1773 ms while a 2381 ms scripted acknowledgment finishes.
issues.cause: Already-speaking acknowledgments and result delivery add latency. Fresh quotation latency also includes the configured local test service: active compute-ms=2500 plus jitter-ms=2000, polled every 500 ms. Phase diagnostic confirms 2852 ms gate wait followed by 4508 ms readiness wait; HTTP requests themselves took only milliseconds.
issues.fix: Candidate keeps only the first cached clause of the exact standard acknowledgment after a naturally completed caller opener; custom text and unrelated turns are unchanged. Quotation polling checks immediately and counts query time in the unchanged interval. Original configuration files and production services remain unchanged.
issues.verified: Both targeted regressions fail on baseline and pass on candidate. Controlled Player output falls from 2380 to 1540 ms (840 ms less); HTTP simulations save 0–502 ms for unchanged readiness/cadence. Six SIP simulations completed but live comparison is inconclusive: receiver TTS warnings, incomplete result-link evidence and neither focused call exercised the scripted acknowledgment. CRM 3201ec4 phase diagnostic archived successfully with zero receiver warnings. Gate wait/API operation/poll sleep measured 2852/4508/4503 ms for a revised quote. Read-only runtime inspection confirms local quotesvc intentional 2500–4500 ms delay; original settings preserved. Full CRM race suite passed in 9.706 s.
issues.effect: Owner explicitly retains the 2500–4500 ms quotation test delay and separates quote completion from the conversational SLA. New qualification uses --quote-sla separate with <1150 ms server p95, >=20 valid conversational responses and unchanged evidence-integrity checks. This diagnostic has only seven valid conversational-content samples after excluding one verified quote-only handoff; no handset qualification. Original configurations remain intact. The five-minute 302267b conversational simulation now passes at 942 ms p95 across 28 valid responses (992 ms with assumed 50 ms overhead); it invokes no quote-result task, so quote-heavy qualification remains separate and incomplete.

issues.title: Silent calling turns lose result timing provenance
issues.symptom: Six explicit result links have output records on the result turn but no playback metric on their originating calling turn. Strict analyzer cannot verify those intervals.
issues.cause: Caller clock and endpoint silence are previously recovered only from calling-turn playback metrics; speculative calling turns may submit a task without ever emitting audio. Further trace inspection shows old ready results can cancel a newer caller turn and start result handling with that newer conversation context (ISS-094). Blindly inheriting the old task origin would therefore risk assigning the wrong caller.
issues.fix: Capture caller-input timing at task submission/coalescing and include versioned numeric provenance on delivery. Analyzer and Journal validate it independently of calling playback, retain evidence failures and do not create conversational samples.
issues.verified: 62 analyzer checks and full Journal race suite pass; baseline public-command regression fails. Recorded 302267b SIP trial validates four captured input links, including silent calling turns. Journal/parser numeric parity verified on the immutable archive at 1150 ms. Five archive files and both audio directions verified; zero receiver warnings. Later 7fc4237 trial validates six direct/coalesced input links but still has one unrooted chained task. Full CI for 302267b passes. Experiment Journal 9916 now runs the CI-passed 302267b parser/UI: 12 archive manifests validate and all 48 raw/transcript files are unchanged across its derived-metadata rebuild.
issues.effect: Direct caller-input provenance is repaired, but two tasks submitted from result turns still lack parent/caller lineage. Keep open. Separate SLA gate fails: conversational p95 1178 ms n=6, two unverified links and two missing quotation readouts. No handset qualification; original configurations, deliberate quote delay and Active Call unchanged. A separate 302267b coverage-question call passes conversational simulator qualification at 942 ms p95 across 28 responses; it invokes no result-delivery tasks and therefore does not close this issue.

issues.title: Old ready result steals a newly finalized caller answer
issues.found_on: Original GoLive SIP simulation and scheduler regression
issues.symptom: An old result starts 42 ms after a newer caller utterance finalizes, before its response plays. The result continuation then launches another task without a direct caller origin.
issues.cause: The result wait deadline measures age from task completion. Once a newer caller finishes speaking, that already-expired deadline can immediately cancel the newer answer, even though its own response window just began.
issues.fix: While an unrelated newer caller answer owns the floor, retain the existing configured delivery wait from that caller endpoint, or until its playback completes. Direct and explicitly coalesced results for that same caller remain eligible immediately. Preserve old acknowledgment cleanup and caller-speech guards.
issues.verified: Baseline regression fails; focused race suite passes in 23.213 s. Recorded 7fc4237 SIP trial exercises protection five times, including measured content on three protected caller turns. Five archive files and both audio directions verified; zero receiver warnings.
issues.effect: Confirmed newer-answer priority now holds within the configured window. Recorded conversational p95 988 ms n=6; strict gate still fails for sample count and one unverified chained result/readout. Quote readout p95 6341 ms n=5 remains separate; original 2500–4500 ms delay and Active Call preserved. Physical handset validation remains outstanding.

retros.sim-conversation-e70c323e-a0eb-4242-b573:
# Conversational SIP comparison: 9547d22

The owner retains the quotation service's deliberate **2500–4500 ms** delay.
Conversational response timing and quotation completion are reported separately.
The server target is strictly below **1150 ms**, using the owner's assumed
50 ms combined telephony/ear allowance for the 1200 ms estimate. These are
simulator results, not physical handset measurements.

Two five-minute, sequential SIP calls used the same original provider profile,
saved prompt/greeting/voice, private CRM snapshot and diagnostic CRM `3201ec4`.
Only the engine build changed: retained original `9547d22` versus `302267b`.
The synthetic customer's 28 coverage/procedure questions replaced the prior
quote-heavy customer scenario; original agent instructions were unchanged.

| Metric | Original `9547d22` | Candidate `302267b` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Conversational responses | 19 | 28 |
| First-audio server p95 | 1017 ms | 934 ms |
| Conversational-content server p95 | 1017 ms | 942 ms |
| Content p95 plus assumed 50 ms | 1067 ms | 992 ms |
| Content maximum | 1017 ms | 1078 ms |
| Simulator receiver first-audio p95 | 1075 ms (18 samples) | 1087 ms (20 samples) |
| Strict separate-SLA gate | Fail | Pass |
| Verified quote-readout samples | 0 | 0 |

The baseline fails for one unverified tool-result link and fewer than 20 valid
responses. The candidate has no missing, unverified, malformed or duplicate
timing records. Both recordings have zero receiver warnings. Four candidate
answers and three baseline answers were interrupted after output began; those
remain counted and labelled in the analyzer rather than discarded.

The candidate's 75 ms lower server-content p95 is an observed difference, not
an isolated causal speedup: generated conversations differed, the baseline
invoked a task and the candidate did not, and the samples are small. Receiver
first-audio p95 did not improve. Server content and receiver first audio are
different measurement boundaries and must not be substituted for each other.

This candidate run meets the conversational simulator gate but does not test
quote-result delivery. The retained quote-heavy `302267b` run still fails with
1178 ms conversational p95 (6 samples), two unverified chained task origins and
two missing quote readouts. That evidence remains visible. A separate trial of
`7fc4237` tests protection of a newer caller answer against an older ready task.

## Retained evidence

- Baseline call: `sim-conversation-e70c323e-a0eb-4242-b573-420c8c18a66a`.
- Candidate call: `sim-conversation-31ed840c-46c6-4282-b339-5c44b55bfc39`.
- Five archive files per call verified against SHA-256 manifests.
- Baseline: 301.596 seconds, 22 assistant / 20 caller transcript entries.
- Candidate: 301.824 seconds, 28 assistant / 28 caller transcript entries.
- Stereo audio contains signal in both channels for both calls.
- Both adapters exit 0; all isolated processes ended after the duration limit.
- Runner operation `conversation-ab-20261101` exits 0 at 14:50:12 on Nov 1.
- Original configuration hashes and Active Call container identity/start match.
- No real call or engine promotion occurred during this operation.

Exact reviewed operations and numeric verification are retained in
[the operation directory](../../scripts/local-ops/recorded/2026-11-01-conversation-ab/).
The native SIP test engine remains `f12b6f5` until a later verified deployment;
the original GoLive engine and Active Call remain available for rollback.

retros.sim-newcaller-16c41c8a-a5b5-413d-ab81-13:
# New caller priority: recorded SIP validation

Call `sim-newcaller-16c41c8a-a5b5-413d-ab81-1377d5891a14` uses engine
`7fc4237`, diagnostic CRM `3201ec4`, the original saved GoLive agent setup,
and the same 90-second quote-heavy customer scenario as the prior `302267b`
trial. Original quote delay remains 2500–4500 ms. No real recipient was dialed.

The scheduler protected a newer caller from an older ready result **five times**.
Three protected turns emitted measured content; two did not and were not given
invented playback samples. The protected item_7 response emitted content
351 ms after its recognized endpoint before the old result took over at the
bounded wait deadline. Item_17 emitted content at 564 ms before the old result
started. Protection is bounded; it does not guarantee uninterrupted completion
of a long answer or solve caller/result lineage on subsequent model tool calls.

| Server metric | p95 | Samples |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First audio | 843 ms | 6 |
| Conversational first content | 988 ms | 6 |
| Linked tool-result content | 8339 ms | 6 |
| Verified quotation readout | 6341 ms | 5 |

The strict separate-SLA gate **fails**: only six conversational responses, one
unverified chained task/result origin and one unverified quotation readout.
There are zero missing readouts among verified links. The assumed handset
content estimate is 1038 ms; no physical handset capture was made.
All six conversational answers were interrupted after output began and remain
included. These limited generated conversations do not establish a causal
speedup over the preceding run (1178 ms conversational p95, six samples).

The trace has six versioned direct/coalesced input links and one unrooted
delivery. Task t5 comes from result turn item_8 after a memory-version change;
it must not inherit an arbitrary old caller clock. ISS-093 remains open.
Recorded ready-result waits reached 4346 ms and 4799 ms during overlapping
caller turns. The deliberate quote service delay and additional result delivery
wait are reported separately; a fast conversational response does not hide them.

Five archive files were hash-verified. The 93.074-second stereo WAV contains
both directions; chat has 13 assistant and 11 caller entries. The receiver
reports zero failures. Adapter exited 0, isolated processes ended, and original
config hashes plus Active Call identity/start were unchanged. The runner exits
0 at 14:52:13 on 2026-11-01. The failed latency gate is recorded independently
of successful execution/archive collection.
